description:
In mta_sts_dns.rs, the id= validation checks len() > 32 and all-alphanumeric, but does NOT reject an empty string. RFC 8461 §3.1 defines id as 1*(%d48-57 / %d65-90 / %d97-122) — one or more characters. An empty id= (from a TXT record like 'v=STSv1; id=') passes both guards because 0 is not > 32 and vacuous all() returns true. The empty id= would then be stored in the cache as the policy_id, breaking rotation detection (any new id= would differ from empty string, triggering unnecessary re-fetches on every delivery).

Fix: add a check if id.is_empty() { return Err(MtaStsError::DnsTxtMissingId); } (or a new DnsTxtIdInvalid, either is reasonable) before or after the length check. Add a test case for id= with empty value.

Severity: P2 — RFC correctness violation; not directly exploitable but causes incorrect behaviour with a malformed TXT record.
title: mta_sts_dns: empty id= accepted (RFC 8461 violation)
